_schema.note: The business being defended. Concrete detail only — staff counts and years trading do more work than any adjective, and they are what makes the closing line land.

fields.name: trading name
fields.profile: one line, factual. Staff, infrastructure, whether they have IT.
fields.years: years trading. Used verbatim in the closure line, so it has to be a number.
fields.stake: what this business cannot operate without. One noun phrase.
fields.comms: inbound messages during a stage, by pressure band. 'from' is a role, never a named person — the player is the one with the name.
fields.survived: shown on the result screen when the business stays open
fields.closed: shown when it does not. This is the emotional peak of the whole asset. Do not make it longer.

clients.name: Harbour Dental
clients.profile: 38 staff, one on-site server, no in-house IT
clients.stake: patient records and the appointment book

calm.text: The system is slow this morning. Is someone doing an update?
We have 41 appointments booked today. Do I need to start calling people?
My login is asking for a code it has never asked for before.

rising.text: I cannot open any patient files. There are six people in the waiting room.
The X-ray software says the server is unreachable. We cannot treat anyone without notes.
Tell me honestly. Is this the kind of thing that ends a business?

critical.text: We are sending patients home. Thirty-one years and we have never done that.
Every file on the shared drive has the same new extension.
There is a message on the screen asking for money. What do I tell the staff?

clients.survived: Harbour Dental opened on time the next morning. The practice owner never had to tell the staff anything.

clients.name: Meridian Logistics
clients.profile: 120 staff, four regional depots, 60 vehicles on the road
clients.stake: the routing system and the customs paperwork

calm.text: Handheld scanners are dropping their connection every few minutes.
Routing is taking twenty seconds to return a job. It is normally instant.
Someone signed into the depot console at 04:00. Nobody was on site.

rising.text: Sixty drivers have no manifests. I am holding them in the yards.
We cannot produce paperwork for the 14:00 crossing. That load is perishable.
Two of our four largest customers have called. What am I allowed to tell them?

critical.text: Nothing here works. We are writing manifests out by hand.
Three loads have been refused at the border for missing documentation.
Our biggest contract has a continuity clause. They are asking me to certify we are operating.

clients.survived: Meridian ran a full schedule the following day. The continuity clause was never invoked.
clients.closed: Meridian Logistics lost its two largest contracts and wound down within the year.

clients.name: Lark & Finch
clients.profile: 24-person accountancy, nine days from the filing deadline
clients.stake: 800 client filings and the working papers behind them

calm.text: Practice software is asking me to reauthenticate. Twice this morning.
The document store is not showing this year's folders. Is it indexing?
A client called about an invoice from us with different bank details.

rising.text: Working papers for 200 clients will not open. The deadline is nine days out.
We hold every client's financial position in there. Is any of it out?
If client data has left the building we have 72 hours to notify. I need to know now.

critical.text: Eight hundred filings. Nine days. I cannot see a way through this.
There is a sample of client data on a leak site. It is real.
Clients are asking whether they should engage someone else for the deadline.

clients.survived: Lark & Finch filed every return on time. No client was ever notified of a breach, because there was nothing to notify.
clients.closed: Lark & Finch missed the deadline for 340 clients and closed after 41 years.

clients.name: Brightwell Surgery
clients.profile: GP practice serving 9,000 patients, two part-time IT days a month
clients.stake: 9,000 patient records and the prescribing system

calm.text: The booking system has logged everyone out twice this morning.
Prescribing is timing out when I try to sign anything.
We had an email about a mandatory update. It came from our own domain.

rising.text: I have a patient in front of me and no history. I need to know what they are on.
Nine thousand records. I have to tell someone if those are gone.
The out-of-hours service is asking us to divert. We have no way to send notes.

critical.text: We are prescribing from memory and patient report. That is not safe and I am recording it.
The regional team have been told. This is a notifiable incident now.
There is a countdown on the reception screen. Patients can see it.

clients.survived: Brightwell held clinic the next morning with full records. The incident was closed without a patient safety report.
clients.closed: Brightwell Surgery's list was dispersed to neighboring practices after 27 years.
